title: Traffic Fraction Composer & Safety DSL for phased model admissions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a declarative Traffic Fraction Composer (TFC) and an accompanying Safety DSL to let PMs/Engineers author phased model admissions: multi-step traffic splits, scheduled step durations, optional shadow probes, cohort targeting, and auto-rollback guardrails. The goal is a single canonical config surface that compiles to runtime routing rules and console UI, supports dry-run validation, and enforces safety constraints (SLO thresholds, error-rate ceilings, regression deltas).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A TFC YAML/JSON schema that expresses: steps (percent), duration, wait conditions, shadow probes, cohort filters, and fallback variants. 2) Server-side compiler that validates policy and emits route spec + telemetry gates. 3) Console editor capable of editing the policy with inline validation and a dry-run simulator. 4) Auto-rollback triggers wired to telemetry (latency p50/p95, error-rate, quality regressions) and a rollback action executed automatically and logged. 5) End-to-end e2e test that runs a seeded canary in staging and exercise rollback flow. 6) Documentation and example policy templates (basic canary, A/B, shadow-only).
technical_notes: We will implement a two-layer approach: 1) A compact DSL (subset of YAML) for authoring; 2) A compiler that converts DSL into low-level route configs consumed by the runtime router. Guardrails will be enforced by a gating service that subscribes to telemetry streams and evaluates guards every evaluation window. To minimize changes in the runtime, the compiled output will use existing versioned routing primitives (route->variant weights, shadow directives) and a control-plane directive for scheduled step activation. The gating service needs access to metric ingest (Prometheus/OTel) and evaluation hooks in the console. Safety policy language must support arithmetic thresholds (e.g., delta>10%), lookback windows, and scoped cohort comparisons.
implementation_plan: - Step 1 (1 week): Design DSL schema and examples; sync with PM/Design; publish spec in Confluence. - Step 2 (2 weeks): Build compiler library in Go, unit tests for schema validation and compile output. - Step 3 (2 weeks): Implement gating service that consumes compiled guard expressions and emits allow/hold/rollback decisions; integrate with telemetry pipeline. - Step 4 (2 weeks): Console UI: editor, dry-run simulation, and rollout timeline visualization. - Step 5 (1 week): Integrate auto-rollback executor with deployment controller and add audit events. - Step 6 (ongoing): E2E tests, staging rollout, and production launch. Each step includes a security/privileged review and a migration plan for existing rollouts.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for DSL parser and compiler (syntactic + semantic checks). - Property tests for guard evaluation (randomized windows). - Integration tests: compile policy -> apply to local router -> simulate traffic using load generator; assert weight transitions and shadowing behavior. - Staging e2e: run a canary on internal models with synthetic regressions injected to validate rollback. - Chaos tests: simulate telemetry lag and partial telemetry loss to ensure gating service errs safe (hold) not unsafe. - UX tests for editor and dry-run simulator.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind 'tfc-experiment' flag; enable for Platform team. 2) Internally run two canaries (non-prod models) for 2 weeks with manual verification. 3) Open beta: allow teams to opt-in; monitor metrics for 14 days. 4) Gradual ramp: enable by default for new model launches with conservative defaults (first step 1% for 30m, second 5% for 2h, then 25%). 5) GA after 6 weeks of stable telemetry and docs. Rollback behavior: gating service will automatically set route to previous stable variant and mark rollout status as 'Auto-Rolled-Back', create an incident artifact, and notify the rollout owner via Slack/email.
monitoring_and_alerts: - Gating evaluations emitted as events (evaluation_id, decision, reason) and stored for audit. - Alert rules: immediate high-priority if auto-rollback triggers; warn if gating holds progress for >2x configured step duration. - Dashboards: per-rollout p50/p95 latency deltas, error-rate, throughput, quality metric divergences (if available). - Tracing: link evaluation events to request traces for root-cause analysis. - Post-rollback job: collect sample requests that triggered the decision and store in secure bucket for evaluation by SRE/Model team.
open_decisions: DSL surface: should we support arbitrary expressions or only a curated predicate set? (trade-off: flexibility vs. auditability)
Rollback action scope: immediate full rollback vs. stepwise retreat? (current plan: immediate rollback to last stable variant)
Metric alignment: using runtime-requested metrics (latency/error) vs. model-specific quality signals (requires instrumentation)
Integration path for Dedicated/Private customers: local telemetry exporters or control-plane webhook?
risks: Telemetry lag can cause false-positive rollbacks; mitigation: require sustained violation windows and conservative defaults.
Overly expressive DSL could allow unsafe policies; mitigation: restrict to audited predicate templates and require code-owner approval for custom predicates.
Auto-rollback could oscillate in flakey networks; mitigation: add cooldown and hysteresis on rollback decisions.
Performance overhead from gating service if evaluation cadence is too high; mitigation: batch evaluations and use approximate summaries for high-traffic rollouts.
